meaning: One email stored as a file. It contains headers a body and any MIME parts or attachments.
example: 000001-fixture.uk.plain.eml

meaning: A reusable test-case definition with known content and expected properties. A fixture can generate one email or a group of related emails.
example: fixture.uk.thread defines three related email files

meaning: A specific version of a fixture chosen by language encoding or deliberate format error.
example: A Japanese notification encoded as UTF-8

meaning: All email files produced by one generate command.
example: 100 .eml files in ./fixtures

meaning: A named group of fixture definitions.
example: core for normal test cases; stress for parser robustness tests

meaning: The list of supported fixtures packs languages and header profiles with their versions.
example: list fixtures --json

meaning: The required JSON input to generate. It sets fixtures file count languages headers seed dates stress permission and limits.
example: batch.astrea-plan.json selects fixture IDs counts seed and languages

meaning: The output index in batch.astrea-manifest.json. It lists generated email files their source fixtures checksums and expected test results.
example: A file uses fixture.us.pdf and should contain one PDF attachment

meaning: A property that a test checks against an expected value.
example: Subject equals Meeting on Friday; Bcc is absent

meaning: An integer that controls generated random values. Same inputs and software versions give the same output.
example: seed: 42 in an .astrea-plan.json file

meaning: A fingerprint of file bytes used to check that content has not changed.
example: sha256 in a manifest entry identifies the exact .eml bytes

meaning: A named set of example headers and formatting rules for a client or provider. Profiles use synthetic values.
example: client.thunderbird.v1 with provider.generic.v1

meaning: A language and regional variant used for text and formatting.
example: en_GB for UK English; ja_JP for Japanese; ar_EG for Arabic

meaning: Right-to-left text direction. Mixed text can also contain left-to-right words or digits.
example: Arabic HTML body with dir=rtl

meaning: The email format rules for text HTML attachments and groups of parts.
example: multipart/alternative holds plain-text and HTML versions

meaning: One item in an email structure: text an attachment an embedded email or a container for other parts.
example: A text/plain part followed by an application/pdf part

meaning: Number of part levels from the root to a part. The root has depth 1.
example: A root container with direct text children has depth 2

meaning: A marker in the file that separates parts inside a multipart container.
example: --astrea-boundary-001

meaning: Character encoding maps text to bytes; transfer encoding represents those bytes inside the email file.
example: UTF-8 text represented using quoted-printable

meaning: An identifier for an embedded part. HTML can refer to an embedded image using a cid: URL.
example: cid:logo@example.test

meaning: Carriage return followed by line feed: the line-ending bytes used in email files.
example: \r\n

meaning: Related emails connected using Message-ID In-Reply-To and References headers.
example: One initial email and two replies

meaning: A deliberately difficult parser test with passive content and limited file size part count and depth.
example: Deeply nested MIME or a missing closing boundary

meaning: A planned direct edit to generated bytes to create a specific format error.
example: Remove a closing MIME boundary

meaning: An email that deliberately breaks a format rule. Its manifest records the intended error.
example: Two conflicting Content-Type headers

meaning: An Astrea identifier for a deliberate format error. A parser may use a different error name.
example: MIME_MISSING_CLOSE

meaning: Exact Python dependency template and profile versions recorded to make generation repeatable.
example: uv.lock plus an exact Python patch version

meaning: The first supported release. Phase 2 Phase 3 and Later describe follow-up work.
example: Core multilingual fixtures and bounded stress fixtures

meaning: Allowed fake hostnames for addresses email identifiers delivery headers and URL examples. Set domains in the plan or read a text file through domain_file.
example: example.test; newletter.test; blue.test
